subject: MSA/Order Form: Aligning auto-renew logic with pilot offboarding — 45/30 split proposal
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acmecorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Evan Lyons <evan.lyons@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on termination for convenience for pilot accounts

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for sending over the order form. Our procurement team is running through the MSA + OF redlines and we hit one item we need to reconcile before we can route to legal: the termination language for pilot accounts (Section 4.2 of the OF draft).

High level: we run short, regional pilots that should be able to exit with standard notice but without a full-term penalty. Specifically, procurement prefers a staggered notice approach: 45 days for enterprise commitments, 30 days for pilot contracts under $50k. That would give us time to offboard and preserve SLAs for active customers while keeping pilots flexible.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood accept a split notice (45/30) carved into the OF and reflected in the MSA as a pilot exception?
- If not, can you propose alternative language that gives pilots a clean opt-out without undermining auto-renew economics?

I included Evan (legal) and procurement alias. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps — we have internal review on Friday.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Questions on termination for convenience for pilot accounts

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the context. Short answer: we're open to a staggered notice window for pilots, but we need to align on three operational points so the economics and rollover behavior don't create spike risk for our dedicated capacity planning:

1) Definition: we should clearly define "pilot account" in the OF (TCV cap, seat/user cap, or trial label) so customers can't broadly classify renewals as pilots.
2) Auto-renew handling: pilots that opt-out at 30 days should not trigger pro-rated credits beyond standard unused prepaid tokens; in other words, no retroactive refunds that undermine committed buckets.
3) Sunset handoff: include a short offboarding SLA (7 business days) for data export and KV cache deletion when pilots exit early.

I'll loop in legal and contracts to draft language. If those three points are acceptable to Acme, we can prepare an annotated redline and a short summary table (45-day for enterprise; 30-day for eligible pilots) for your Friday review.

Propose a quick 20-min sync Thu 11:00 PT if that works.

Best,

Team —

Acme is asking for a staggered 45/30 notice split. See Olivia's note below. They want pilot accounts under $50k to be able to exit with 30 days. Evan (Acme legal) is cc'd.

Quick asks: can legal draft clean MSA + OF language to capture:
- Pilot definition (suggest: "Pilot Account" = Order Forms with total committed consideration < $50,000 and explicitly labeled "Pilot" on the Order Form);
- Termination for Convenience (TFC) carve-out that allows 30-day notice for Pilot Accounts but preserves auto-renew for enterprise orders at 45 days;
- Offboarding SLA: 7 business days for data export, and clear statement that cached artifacts are deleted;
- Explicit statement that early pilot exits do not create refunds for previously consumed compute/seat credits, only unused pre-paid credits per OF billing terms.

Marissa/Laura: can you prioritize a redline + a short matrix (we can send to procurement) by EOD Thursday? Mina, any legal concerns on carving out pilots while keeping the auto-renew for enterprise intact?

Thanks —
Karthik

Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 14:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on termination for convenience for pilot accounts — redline attached

Thanks Karthik — I put together a redline and a short matrix that captures the operational constraints we discussed. Key points in the attached:

- Pilot definition: Order Form must include an explicit field labeled "Pilot Account" and total committed consideration < $50,000; otherwise default to enterprise terms.
- TFC language (MSA §7.1 / OF §4.2): "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, a Customer may terminate a Pilot Account upon 30 days' prior written notice. All other Order Forms and agreements shall continue to be governed by the standard 45-day termination notice required for auto-renewed commitments."
- Billing: early termination will not entitle Customer to refunds for consumed prepaid tokens or usage; refunds only apply to unused prepaid, unallocated credits as of termination date per OF billing schedule.
- Offboarding SLA: Redwood will provide data export within 7 business days and will confirm deletion of customer-specific cache and temporary artifacts within 10 business days.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline annotated), autorenew_staggered_matrix.xlsx (matrix: scenarios + accounting impact).

Mina — flagging two legal questions in the redline: (1) do we need a cap on the number of pilot terminations in a rolling 12-month window to prevent abuse? (2) should pilot accounts be excluded from certain SLAs if they opt-out early? I added suggested language but would like legal signoff.

If Olivia/Evan are good with this we can prepare a clean OF for signature and a short email that explains the operational protections.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Olivia / Evan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review, attached is the proposed redline that implements the 45/30 split for termination notice with the operational guards you requested. Summary of what changed vs. your ask:

- Implemented Pilot Account definition and explicit labeling requirement on the Order Form (prevents broader reclassification).
- 30-day TFC for Pilot Accounts; 45-day TFC for all other Order Forms.
- Billing mechanics clarified: no refunds for consumed prepaid tokens; unused prepaid credits handled per OF schedule.
- Offboarding: 7 business day data export guarantee; confirmation of cache deletion within 10 business days.
- Abuse mitigation: up to 3 pilot-term exits allowed per rolling 12-month period; additional exits require sales approval. (Legal suggested this cap to limit churn risk.)

If that reflects Acme's needs, I've initiated a DocuSign envelope for the clean Order Form and a one‑page summary that you can circulate to procurement. Link: https://docusign.com/ACME-PO-47

If you'd like to discuss the 3-exit cap, Marissa and Mina are available Monday morning.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly so engineering can schedule the pilot.

Best,
